title: Check security, privacy and data protection
summary: Before real users and real data arrive, check that the product protects both. Security and privacy problems found after launch are expensive and damage trust.

beginner: List what personal or sensitive data the product collects, where it is stored and who can see it.
Check you only collect what you need, and that users are told how it is used.
Ask your security colleague or a specialist to check the product against common risks, such as the OWASP Top Ten.
Check who can access what: users should only see their own data, and staff only what they need.
Complete a data protection impact assessment if the processing is high risk.
Fix serious issues before launch and record any accepted risks with an owner.
intermediate: Map personal data flows and check minimisation and transparency.
Arrange a security review or penetration test proportionate to the risk.
Complete a data protection impact assessment where needed and track fixes.
experienced: Build security and privacy reviews into the delivery process, not just before launch.
Threat-model new features with engineering early.
Agree risk acceptance rules with security and legal leaders.
Plan for data subject requests, retention and deletion from the start.

canDelegateTo.task: Lead the data protection impact assessment
Fix security issues and check access controls

toolExamples.github: Turn on secret scanning and dependency alerts for the repository.
toolExamples.gitlab: Use security scanning in the pipeline so issues are found on every change.
toolExamples.aws: Review access permissions so each service has only what it needs.
toolExamples.azure: Review access permissions so each service has only what it needs.
toolExamples.gcp: Review access permissions so each service has only what it needs.
toolExamples.confluence: Keep the data map and the impact assessment together on one page.

definitionOfDone: Security review done and serious issues fixed
pitfalls: Leaving security to the last week
Collecting data 'in case it is useful'
Assuming the hosting provider handles everything
